name: Digital Nomad Visa
income_type: Remote employment income for a foreign (non-Italian) employer
requirements: Remote employment contract or freelance/business with non-Italian clients
Income proof ≥€24,789/year
Bachelor's degree OR professional government license OR 5+ years relevant experience
Health insurance covering minimum €30,000 (approximately $35,000 USD)
Housing lease or contract in Italy in your name
Employer letter confirming no immigration law violations
Clean criminal background (FBI background check apostilled)
apply_at: Italian Consulate in your jurisdiction (before travel)
family: Spouse and children under 18 can be sponsored after you arrive
path_to_residency: After 5 years of legal residence, eligible to apply for permanent residence. After 10 years, citizenship.
tax_implications: As a tax resident, you'd file Italian taxes on worldwide income. Consult a cross-border US-Italy tax specialist — the US-Italy tax treaty prevents double taxation.
airbnb_compatibility: ✅ As a registered tax resident, you can operate Airbnb under the cedolare secca 21% flat tax regime.
pros: Only 1-year initial commitment — test Italy before committing
Lower income threshold than Elective Residency
Renewable annually as long as employment continues
cons: Must maintain remote foreign-employer income to renew
Must file Italian taxes (requires cross-border tax planning)
If you change jobs to an Italian employer, visa becomes void

name: Schengen 90-Day Rule
requirements: US passport valid ≥3 months beyond planned stay
Sufficient funds (no specific threshold but customs may ask)
Return/onward ticket
apply_at: No application needed — enter at border
family: Family members apply individually on their US passports
path_to_residency: This does NOT lead to residency — only visa-free tourism
tax_implications: As a non-resident, you owe Italian tax only on Italian-sourced income (i.e., your Airbnb rental income). This is auto-withheld by Airbnb at 21%.
airbnb_compatibility: ✅ Non-residents can legally operate Airbnb in Italy. CIN registration is required regardless of residency status.
pros: Available immediately — use for scouting trips
No paperwork, no application, no fees
Can purchase property in Italy with no visa
90 days is enough for 2–3 long trips per year
cons: Cannot legally reside in Italy beyond 90 days in any 180-day period
Cannot work, even remotely, on a tourist entry
Property must be managed remotely or via property manager
note: Use the Schengen days calculator at visa-calculator.com to track your remaining days. Overstaying can result in a 1–5 year Schengen ban.

name: Elective Residency Visa
duration: 1 year, renewable — leads to permanent residency after 5 years
your_income: Income MUST be passive — pensions, dividends, rental income, royalties
income_type: PASSIVE income only — employment salary does NOT qualify
requirements: Passive income ≥€31,000/year (employment income excluded)
Proof of stable long-term income (rental, investment, pension)
Italian property or 1-year rental contract
Italian health insurance (€30,000 coverage minimum)
FBI background check apostilled
No intention to work in Italy
path_to_residency: Direct path to permanent residency after 5 years, then citizenship after 10 years
tax_implications: Full Italian tax resident — must declare worldwide income. The 7% flat tax regime for retirees could apply IF income is from pension/passive sources.
airbnb_compatibility: ✅ As an Italian tax resident with this visa, you can legally operate Airbnb.
pros: No requirement to work at all
Opens the door to the 7% flat tax regime
Best visa for early retirees or those with rental income
cons: Your current employment income does NOT qualify
Only viable once you have €31,000+/year in passive income
Strategy: build Airbnb income over time, then transition to this visa
May need 3–5 years of Airbnb + investment income before qualifying
strategy: LONG-TERM PLAN: Once your Italian Airbnb + US investment/dividend income exceeds €31,000/year, you could transition from Digital Nomad Visa to Elective Residency. This would make permanent Italy residency possible even without employment.

name: Investor Visa (Golden Visa)
requirements: €250,000 investment in Italian innovative startup, OR
€500,000 investment in Italian company, OR
€1,000,000 philanthropic donation, OR
€2,000,000 Italian government bonds
apply_at: Italian Ministry of Economic Development (pre-clearance required)
path_to_residency: Yes — can lead to permanent residency
tax_implications: Variable depending on tax residency election
cons: €250,000 minimum investment — far exceeds current savings (~$100K)
Not viable without significantly more capital
